# The scoreboard: ISLA against GeoTransolver and Transolver {#sec-scoreboard}

**With every architecture fed the same inputs and scored on the same
float32 instrument at the reporting protocol of 200,000 cells per case,
ISLA and GeoTransolver are at parity on DrivAerML at full data
(GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA 0.998) and ISLA leads Transolver by 6%; below full
data GeoTransolver holds a data-efficiency lead that narrows from 17% at 27
cars to zero at 435; on HiLiftAeroML GeoTransolver and Transolver lead by
27 to 31% on the 35-case and fixed-angle rungs at either budget. ISLA leads
where every case arrives in its own random pose (by 12% over GeoTransolver
and 21% over Transolver), on interior velocity (by 42%), under a change of
the law the training sample is drawn by (GeoTransolver and Transolver
trained on the area-proportional draw are 2.6 to 7.9x worse on the uniform
one, ISLA 1 to 8%), and on the accuracy-against-memory frontier, where its
best configuration at or under each training-memory budget is at least as
accurate as GeoTransolver's at every budget measured and 9% more accurate
at 40 GB. Given width and depth, both architectures reach the same floor of
about 0.040 on DrivAerML, ISLA at 68 to 136M parameters and GeoTransolver
at 143 to 571M.** This chapter is the standing on one page. The
cross-architecture measurements of the book appear here as boards computed
from the same result files the evidence chapters use, so a reader who needs
the standing and not the derivation can stop after this chapter and go to
@sec-data-efficiency, @sec-full-data, @sec-interior and
@sec-baselines only for the protocol behind a particular row.
The rungs not yet measured at the reporting protocol are listed at the end
(@sec-scoreboard-exploration).

## How to read every number {#sec-scoreboard-protocol}

- **The metric** is the area-weighted relative L2 error of surface pressure
  (@sec-metrics), averaged over the validation cases of the split, from a
  float32 inference on the final-epoch checkpoint. Interior rows use the same
  error on interior pressure, velocity and eddy viscosity.
- **The inputs are matched.** Every model receives the freestream as a unit
  direction (the unit-direction protocol, @sec-fair-comparison); tokens per
  case, epochs (500), split and validation cases are identical across
  architectures in every row, and each architecture runs at its own best
  learning rate. GeoTransolver's best rate depends on how much data it sees
  (3e-3 at 200,000 cells on every DrivAerML rung and on the wings, 1e-3 at
  10,000 cells at full data on the cars); the rows name the rate used.
- **One reporting protocol.** Every standing is measured at the recipe's
  default of 200,000 sampled cells per case (@sec-scoreboard-200k). The
  program explored at 10,000 cells before adopting it; a 10,000-cell number
  appears in this chapter only as a rung of a cell-count ladder, labeled
  *exploration budget*, and never as a standing. On DrivAerML the full-data
  gap that the smaller count shows is count noise (@sec-deficit-anatomy);
  on the wing rungs the count changes nothing. The capacity and memory
  results were measured at 100,000 cells, a *scaling budget* labeled as
  such; every model's error is flat in the cell count above 100,000
  (@sec-scoreboard-tokens).
- **A ratio is baseline error divided by ISLA error**, so a value above one
  favors ISLA. Seeds do not measure the choice of training cases; on the 35-
  and 210-case wing rungs the uncertainty to read is the spread over random
  training draws, three to eleven times the seed spread (@sec-de-controls).
- **Which ISLA.** Every ISLA number in this chapter's figures and tables is
  ISLA (relative frame, @sec-isla); the surface rows were trained with the
  total-measure length unit, within 0.4% of the RMS-pairwise-distance
  default at the reporting protocol (@sec-nb-lenrms-200k). The legacy
  centered variant and the similarity-gauge variant, both removed from the
  class, appear only in collapsed diagnostic notes, labeled.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="The detail behind those rules"}
Learning rates: at the reporting protocol GeoTransolver's better rate is
3e-3 on every DrivAerML rung and on the wings, and it was 1e-3 at 10,000
cells at full data on the cars; Transolver runs at 3e-3 everywhere; ISLA
at 1e-3 at width 192 and the width rule above it (@sec-using-lr). At 1,260
wing cases GeoTransolver and the legacy centered variant (diagnostic) were
trained at 10,000 and at 20,000 cells: each improves by about 5% and their
ratio does not move (@sec-nb-w2c-floor-verdict). One further family of
configurations appears where it informs the reading: GeoTransolver and
Transolver with the surface measure carried in their slice pooling,
ablations that locate a property (the public models are not modified,
@sec-part-baseline).
:::

## The standing at the reporting protocol: 200,000 cells {#sec-scoreboard-200k}

**At the reporting protocol, the recipe's default of 200,000 sampled cells
per case, ISLA and GeoTransolver are at parity on DrivAerML at full data
(0.998), ISLA leads Transolver by 6%, below full data GeoTransolver holds a
data-efficiency lead that narrows from 17% at 27 cars to zero at 435, and
on the two HiLiftAeroML rungs measured GeoTransolver and Transolver lead by
21 to 31%.** This is the book's primary standing. The DrivAerML table is
computed from the 200,000-cell artifacts and names GeoTransolver's rate on
every row, because GeoTransolver's best rate depends on how much data it
sees: 3e-3 beats 1e-3 by 31%, 24%, 10%, 4% and 2% at 27, 54, 109, 218 and
435 cars at this budget, where 1e-3 had won its 435-car grid at 10,000
cells (@sec-nb-rategt-prereg, @sec-nb-proto200k-verdict). ISLA has one
usable rate under linear routing (1e-3 at width 192; @sec-robustness-lr)
and Transolver runs at 3e-3 throughout. A row would mark itself
*provisional* if a rate control were still training; none is.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scoreboard-200k
#| output: asis
P2 = J("p200k_trio_reduction_2026-09-19.json"); L2 = J("p200k_ladder_interim_2026-09-18.json")
out = "| DrivAerML training cars | ISLA (1e-3) | GeoTransolver (better of 1e-3, 3e-3) | Transolver (3e-3) | GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA | Transolver ÷ ISLA | status |\n|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|\n"
for n in ("n27", "n54", "n109", "n218"):
    r = L2["rungs"][n]; isla = r["isla"]["pressure_mean"]; g1 = r["gt_unit"]
    rc = r.get("rate_control_lr3e3", {}).get("gt_unit_lr3e3")
    if rc and rc["pressure_mean"] < g1["pressure_mean"]:
        g, glab, status = rc, "3e-3", "final"
    elif rc:
        g, glab, status = g1, "1e-3", "final"
    else:
        g, glab, status = g1, "1e-3", "provisional: 3e-3 control training"
    t = r["transolver_unit"]
    out += (f"| {n[1:]} | {isla:.4f} | {g['pressure_mean']:.4f} ({glab}) | {t['pressure_mean']:.4f} | {g['pressure_mean']/isla:.2f} | {t['pressure_mean']/isla:.2f} | {status} |\n")
A = P2["arms"]; isla = A["isla"]["pressure_mean"]
gts = {k: A[k]["pressure_mean"] for k in ("gt_unit_lr1e3", "gt_unit_lr3e3") if A[k]["pressure_mean"] and A[k]["n"] == 2}
best = min(gts, key=gts.get); glab = "3e-3" if best.endswith("3e3") else "1e-3"
status = "final" if "gt_unit_lr3e3" in gts else "provisional: 3e-3 control training"
out += (f"| **435** | **{isla:.4f}** | **{gts[best]:.4f}** ({glab}) | **{A['transolver_unit_lr3e3']['pressure_mean']:.4f}** | **{gts[best]/isla:.2f}** | **{A['transolver_unit_lr3e3']['pressure_mean']/isla:.2f}** | {status} |\n")
print(out)
print(": Surface-pressure error (area-weighted relative L2, float32, 48 DrivAerML validation cars) with every model trained and "
      "scored at 200,000 sampled cells per case, width 192 (ISLA) and 256 (GeoTransolver, Transolver), 500 epochs, two seeds (seed means; the per-seed values are in the "
      "artifacts). GeoTransolver's column takes the better of its 1e-3 and 3e-3 pairs and names the rate; a row marked provisional "
      "still awaits that control. ISLA carries the total-measure length unit in these lanes; the RMS-pairwise-distance unit, now "
      "the default, scores 0.0444 on the same 435-car protocol (0.996 of it, @sec-nb-lenrms-200k). How to read this: ratios above 1 favor ISLA. Data: "
      "results/p200k_trio_reduction_2026-09-19.json; results/p200k_ladder_interim_2026-09-18.json. {#tbl-scoreboard-200k}")
```

```{python}
      f"{'' if gt_final else '; GeoTransolver’s 3e-3 pair is still training and the row is provisional'}. "

      f"({(1-P2['verdict']['isla_200k_over_10k'])*100:.0f}% against {(1-gts[best]/tenk['gt_unit'])*100:.0f}% for GeoTransolver and "
      f"{(1-A['transolver_unit_lr3e3']['pressure_mean']/tenk['transolver_unit'])*100:.0f}% for Transolver), which is the count-noise term of the deficit anatomy "
      f"(@sec-deficit-anatomy) going to zero at the denser sampling. Below full data GeoTransolver at its better rate "
      f"leads ISLA by {', '.join(f'{(1-r)*100:.0f}%' for r in lads)} at 27, 54, 109 and 218 cars, a deficit that closes at the full training set. "
      f"On the wings the budget changes nothing (@tbl-scoreboard-200k-wings): on the 35-case rung GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA is 0.73 at 200,000 cells against 0.72 at 10,000, "
      f"and on the fixed-angle rung 0.69 against 0.68, so the wing deficit is a property of the trained functions, not of the sampling count.")
```

```{python}
print(": The 35-case and fixed-angle HiLiftAeroML rungs at both budgets, and the 4-geometry rung at the reporting protocol (surface-pressure error, float32, 180 validation cases, seed means; GeoTransolver at 3e-3 in both protocols, its better rate on these rungs; the 10,000-cell rows are rungs of the cell-count ladder, not standings). "
      "How to read this: on the 35-case rung twenty times the sampled cells moved neither model by more than 4%, and on the fixed-angle rung every model improved by 20% to 25% while the ratios moved by 0.01 and 0.04, so the wing deficit is not count noise; the mechanism the program points at is the mesher pattern where validation geometries recur in training (@sec-data-efficiency). "
      f"The other wing rungs ({len(pending)} of them) are training at 200,000 cells and join this table as they report (@sec-program-status). Data: results/p200k_fleet_reduction_2026-09-19.json; results/p200k_fleet_interim_2026-09-20.json; "
      "results/fp32_reeval/fp32_shift_35_2026-09-09.json; results/relframe_reduction_2026-09-11.json. {#tbl-scoreboard-200k-wings}")
```

## Interior fields from the surface {#sec-scoreboard-interior}

**On the boundary-to-interior task at the reporting protocol (200,000
boundary cells and 200,000 interior queries per car) ISLA, with its interior
queries admitted as interacting tokens and given the signed distance to the
wall, is 42% more accurate than GeoTransolver-volume on interior velocity at
a third of the parameters, 13% less accurate on interior pressure and level
on eddy viscosity; with cosine routing the velocity lead is 56% and the
pressure deficit 5%.** The task, the two architectures' interior modes and
the diagnostics are in @sec-interior. This is a single-dataset result: the
interior task has no wing twin. Two conditions travel with the rows. With
400,000 interacting tokens per car ISLA's interior configuration under
linear routing rises to the mean-field loss plateau at the surface
configuration's rate of 1e-3 (both seeds, the routing saturation of
@sec-using-lr) and trains cleanly at 5e-4, the rate the linear row uses;
3e-4 is 3% to 8% worse. Cosine routing, which bounds the routing logits
(@sec-isla-slices), trains at 1e-3 and gives the better row. Every interior
lane was trained with the passive readout's `query_mass="geometric_mean"`
option; the class default is now `"source_total"`, and the count dependence
under it is not measured (@sec-interior-companion). GeoTransolver-volume
trains at 1e-3 at this count.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scoreboard-200k-interior
#| output: asis
fields = [("pressure_l2", "interior pressure"), ("velocity_l2", "interior velocity"), ("nut_l2", "eddy viscosity")]
RV = J("ratevol_reduction_2026-09-20.json"); rva = RV["arms"]
EXTI = J("routenorm_extension_2026-09-21.json")["configurations"]["isla|cos|interior|w192|lr1e-3"]
gtv200 = {f: rva["gt_vol_unit"][f]["mean"] for f, _ in fields}
def rrow(label, vals, ref=None):
    cells = []
    for f, _ in fields:
        m = vals[f]; cells.append(f"{m:.4f}" + (f" ({ref[f]/m:.2f})" if ref else ""))
    return f"| {label} | " + " | ".join(cells) + " |\n"
def arm(a): return {f: rva[a][f]["mean"] for f, _ in fields}
out = "| arm, 435 training cars, 200,000 cells and queries | pressure | velocity | eddy viscosity |\n|---|---|---|---|\n"
out += rrow("GeoTransolver-volume, 27.6M, unit direction, 1e-3", gtv200)
out += rrow("ISLA, query tokens + signed distance, 8.9M, linear routing, 5e-4 (GeoTransolver-volume ÷ ISLA)", arm("isla_lr5e4"), gtv200)
out += rrow("**ISLA, query tokens + signed distance, 8.9M, cosine routing, 1e-3 (ratio)**", {f: EXTI[f"{f}_mean"] for f, _ in fields}, gtv200)
out += rrow("ISLA, linear routing, 3e-4, rate control (ratio)", arm("isla_lr3e4"), gtv200)
out += rrow("ISLA, linear routing, 1e-3, on the mean-field plateau (ratio)", arm("isla_lr1e3"), gtv200)
print(out)
b = RV["bars"]
print(": Interior error at the reporting protocol (relative L2 over the 48 DrivAerML validation cars, float32, two seeds, "
      "200,000 boundary cells and 200,000 interior queries per car, 500 epochs). Ratios in parentheses are "
      "GeoTransolver-volume ÷ ISLA (above 1 favors ISLA). Against the same arms trained and scored at 10,000 queries the linear row's "
      f"velocity ratio moved {b['velocity_l2']['relative_change']*100:+.1f}% (within the preregistered 5%) and its pressure ratio "
      f"{b['pressure_l2']['relative_change']*100:+.1f}%, a swing inside ISLA's 8% seed spread on pressure "
      f"({' / '.join(f'{v:.4f}' for v in rva['isla_lr5e4']['pressure_l2']['seeds'])}); the cosine row's pressure seeds are "
      f"{' / '.join(f'{v:.4f}' for v in EXTI['pressure_l2_seeds'])}. The 1e-3 linear row is the plateau signature, kept as the "
      "record of the rate ceiling (@sec-nb-ratevol-verdict). How to read this: single dataset (the interior task has no wing twin); "
      "every ISLA lane here uses the passive readout's geometric-mean query mass, not the class default. "
      "Data: results/ratevol_reduction_2026-09-20.json; results/routenorm_extension_2026-09-21.json. {#tbl-scoreboard-200k-interior}")
```

The interacting decode's prediction at a point depends on the joint query
set, so each interior value holds at its own training count
(@sec-interior-companion).

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Interior rows measured only on the similarity-gauge variant (removed variant; pending on ISLA at the reporting protocol)"}
The interior program was built on the similarity-gauge variant
(measure-weighted centroid and RMS-radius length unit) before the relative
frame replaced it and the variant was removed from the class; it read a
center estimated from the sample, so it appears only here. Two of its
measurements have no ISLA twin at any budget: the width-344 arm that
matches GeoTransolver-volume's 27.6M parameters, and the 54- and 109-car
rungs. Both were measured at 10,000 boundary cells and 10,000 queries
(results/fp32_reeval/fp32_shift_interior_2026-09-09.json;
research/transfer_program/studies/computational_support/campaign_d_verdict_2026-09-10.json)
and are pending on ISLA at the reporting protocol; their values are not
quoted. The orderings they gave, stated in @sec-interior-open, are
mechanism readings on the removed variant and not rows.
:::

## Arbitrary poses: where the contract earns accuracy {#sec-scoreboard-pose}

**When every training and validation case arrives in its own random
orientation, ISLA's error moves by 1.5% and the augmented baselines' rises
by 12% and 16%, which makes ISLA 12% and 21% more accurate than
GeoTransolver and Transolver on the same posed cars at the reporting
protocol.** This is ISLA's one measured in-distribution accuracy lead over
input-matched baselines on the surface, and it is conditional on the
setting: in a canonical frame GeoTransolver is at parity
(@sec-scoreboard-200k), and GeoTransolver trained in a canonicalized frame
is pose-invariant at a 1% cost (@sec-pose). ISLA's rotation and translation
covariance is exact by construction (@sec-isla-contracts) and needs no
augmentation; the same checkpoints scored in the native frame land within
0.5% of their posed numbers (@sec-nb-poseref-verdict).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scoreboard-pose-200k
#| output: asis
PP = J("p200k_pose_reduction_2026-09-19.json"); NAT = PP["native_frame_reference"]
def seeds2(a): return " / ".join(f"{v['pressure_l2']:.4f}" for v in a["per_seed"].values())
out = "| architecture | native frame | every case in a random pose | posed ÷ native | baseline ÷ ISLA, posed |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n"
for label, key in (("GeoTransolver, trained with rotation augmentation (native at 1e-3)", "gt_unit"), ("Transolver, trained with rotation augmentation", "transolver_unit"), ("ISLA, no augmentation", "isla")):
    a = PP["arms"][key]
    out += f"| {label} | {NAT[key]:.4f} | {a['posed_mean']:.4f} ({seeds2(a)}) | {a['posed_over_native']:.3f} | {a['posed_mean']/PP['arms']['isla']['posed_mean']:.2f} |\n"
print(out)
print(": The pose test at the reporting protocol: DrivAerML surface pressure, 435 training cars, 48 validation cars, 200,000 cells, float32, two seeds each. "
      "The native column is each architecture's error in the dataset's frame from @tbl-scoreboard-200k (GeoTransolver's posed lanes ran at 1e-3, so its native reference here is the 1e-3 pair); the posed column trains and validates with every case rotated by its own random rotation. "
      "How to read this: the last column is the posed comparison, ratios above 1 favor ISLA; the native column is the canonical-frame standing, where GeoTransolver is at parity. "
      "Data: results/p200k_pose_reduction_2026-09-19.json; results/p200k_trio_reduction_2026-09-19.json. {#tbl-scoreboard-pose-200k}")
```

## Consistency under a change of surface sampling {#sec-scoreboard-consistency}

**Every configuration that centers its coordinates on a statistic of the
sampled points, whichever architecture it belongs to, degrades 5 to 9x at
100,000 cells when the same surface is resampled with a 10:1 front-to-back
density bias; ISLA, whose frame reads nothing from the sample, holds at
1.07x, and GeoTransolver and Transolver join that group once their datapipe
centers on an unbiased estimate of the geometric centroid (an ablation
measured in the exploration runs and pending at this budget).**
Consistency in the fine-mesh limit is
the acceptance criterion of @sec-principle, not a score: a model whose
prediction depends on where the mesher happened to refine is not predicting
the physics. The probe holds the geometry fixed and redraws the cells with
the bias, with exact Horvitz–Thompson weights, the inverse of each cell's
inclusion probability under the draw, so a measure-consistent model sees the
same surface integral; the ratio of the error under the biased draw to the
error under the uniform draw is the number in @fig-scoreboard-density,
stated in the sample frame, the frame a biased mesher would deliver.

```{python}
#| label: fig-scoreboard-density
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Sampling-density sensitivity by architecture on DrivAerML at the
#|   scaling budget (435 training cars, 48 validation cars, 100,000 cells,
#|   float32, two seeds, the uniform-trained checkpoints of the training-law
#|   study): surface-pressure error under the 10:1 front/back biased draw
#|   divided by the same checkpoint's error under the uniform draw, on a log
#|   axis; 1 is exact consistency and the gray band marks up to 1.5x. Bars
#|   are sample-frame values, in which every model's input is centered on
#|   the drawn points. Color follows the book's key: ISLA blue,
#|   GeoTransolver red, Transolver amber. How to read this: a bar near 1
#|   means the architecture's answer does not depend on the sampling law at
#|   this count; it does not rank in-distribution accuracy, which is in
#|   @tbl-scoreboard-200k, and it does not show the ablations of
#|   GeoTransolver and Transolver with ISLA's measure-weighted pooling and a
#|   Horvitz–Thompson-centered datapipe, which were measured in the
#|   exploration runs and are pending at this budget
#|   (@sec-robustness-density). Data:
#|   results/trainarea_dr_reduction_2026-09-20.json.
#| code-fold: true
TD = J("trainarea_dr_reduction_2026-09-20.json")["arms"]
R = MAT["rows"]  # per-configuration rows of the accuracy/consistency matrix, used by the diagnostic notes below
items = [("ISLA", "isla", "isla_ref"), ("GeoTransolver", "gt_unit", "gt"), ("Transolver", "transolver_unit", "t")]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9.0, 3.2))
y = list(range(len(items)))[::-1]
ax.axvspan(1.0, 1.5, color=GRID, alpha=0.7, zorder=0)
for yy, (label, m, k) in zip(y, items):
    u = TD[f"{m}_uniform"]["mean"]; sf = u["biased"] / u["unif"]
    ax.barh(yy, sf, height=0.62, zorder=2, **bar_kwargs(k))
    ax.text(sf * 1.06, yy, f"{sf:.2f}x", va="center", fontsize=8.5, color=INK2)
ax.set_yticks(y); ax.set_yticklabels([i[0] for i in items], fontsize=9)
ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_xlim(0.9, 20)
ax.set_xticks([1, 1.5, 2, 5, 10]); ax.set_xticklabels(["1", "1.5", "2", "5", "10"])
ax.xaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter())
ax.axvline(1.0, color=INK2, lw=1.0, zorder=1)
ax.set_xlabel("error under 10:1 biased sampling ÷ error under uniform sampling [–], scaling budget (100,000 cells)\n(sample frame: each model's input frame taken from the drawn points)", fontsize=9.5)
ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

@tbl-scoreboard-density-100k puts the biased draw beside the stratified
one at the same count: the stratified draw, which keeps the sampling law
and only spreads the cells, moves every model by under 2%, so the biased
column measures the law and not the noise.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scoreboard-density-100k
#| output: asis
out = "| model | 100,000 cells: biased ÷ uniform | 100,000 cells: stratified ÷ uniform |\n|---|---:|---:|\n"
for label, m in (("ISLA", "isla"), ("GeoTransolver", "gt_unit"), ("Transolver", "transolver_unit")):
    u = TD[f"{m}_uniform"]["mean"]
    out += f"| {label} | {u['biased']/u['unif']:.2f}x | {u['strat']/u['unif']:.2f}x |\n"
print(out)
print(": The inference-draw change at 100,000 cells on DrivAerML (435 training cars, 48 validation cars, float32, seed means): surface-pressure error under the 10:1 front/back "
      "biased draw, and under the stratified draw, divided by the same checkpoint's error under the independent uniform draw, every draw with exact "
      "Horvitz–Thompson weights, on the uniform-trained checkpoints of the training-law study (@sec-training-law), each architecture at its reporting-protocol rate. How to read this: 1 is exact "
      "consistency; the stratified column shows that a draw under the same law moves every model by under 2%, so the biased column measures the law and not the noise. "
      "Data: results/trainarea_dr_reduction_2026-09-20.json. {#tbl-scoreboard-density-100k}")
```

The single-count probe understates the question the principle asks, which
is whether the prediction converges to one field as the sample is refined
and to the same field under two sampling laws. The consistency benchmark of
@sec-consistency-bench evaluates every checkpoint at 2,500 to 40,000 cells
under three samplers; @tbl-scoreboard-bench reads it at 40,000 cells, where
a consistent configuration is within 3% of its own uniform-sampling answer.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scoreboard-bench
#| output: asis
def bench(path): return J("consistency_bench/" + path)["arms"]
B0, Bmw, Bmc, Brf = (bench("consistency_bench_2026-09-10.json"), bench("consistency_bench_mw_2026-09-10.json"),
                     bench("consistency_bench_mcenter_2026-09-10.json"), bench("consistency_bench_rf_2026-09-11.json"))
def D(arms, arm, sampler, count="40000"):
    t = arms[arm]["table"]; return t[sampler][count]["pressure_l2"]["mean"] / t["unif"][count]["pressure_l2"]["mean"] - 1
def cell(arms, arm):
    return f"{D(arms, arm, 'area'):+.0%} / {D(arms, arm, 'biased'):+.0%}"
rows = [
    ("ISLA", "in-model, none", (Brf, "rf_dr_mt2_meas"), (Brf, "rf_hl_mt2_meas_super_scarce")),
    ("GeoTransolver", "pipeline pool mean (unbiased)", (B0, "uw_gt_unit_lr1e3"), (B0, "udrv_hl_gt_super_scarce_lr3e3")),
    ("Transolver", "pipeline pool mean (unbiased)", (B0, "uw_transolver_unit_lr3e3"), (B0, "udrv_hl_transolver_super_scarce_lr3e3")),
    ("GeoTransolver + ISLA's measure-weighted pooling (ablation)", "pipeline pool mean (unbiased)", (Bmw, "mw_dr_gt_unit_lr1e3"), (Bmw, "mw_hl_gt_super_scarce_lr3e3")),
    ("Transolver + ISLA's measure-weighted pooling (ablation)", "pipeline pool mean (unbiased)", (Bmw, "mw_dr_transolver_unit_lr3e3"), (Bmw, "mw_hl_transolver_super_scarce_lr3e3")),
]
out = "| configuration | frame convention in the benchmark | DrivAerML: area / biased | HiLift 35 cases: area / biased |\n|---|---|---:|---:|\n"
for label, frame, dr, hl in rows:
    out += f"| {label} | {frame} | {cell(*dr)} | {cell(*hl) if hl else 'not run'} |\n"
print(out)
print(": Sampling-distribution dependence at 40,000 cells, float32, two seeds, checkpoints trained at the exploration budget: the change in "
      "surface-pressure error when the same surface is drawn proportionally to cell area (area) or "
      "with the 10:1 front/back bias (biased) instead of uniformly over cells, as a percentage of the "
      "uniform-draw error; within ±3% counts as consistent. The frame column states where each "
      "model's input frame came from in this benchmark: GeoTransolver and Transolver received their center from the "
      "pipeline's uniform 320,000-cell pool before the draw, an unbiased frame that a biased mesher "
      "would not deliver (their sample-frame sensitivity is the bar in @fig-scoreboard-density), while "
      "ISLA computes its frame in the model from the drawn points. How to read this: with the frame held, measure "
      "weighting makes the baselines' aggregation consistent; the frame is the separate defect. Data: "
      "results/consistency_bench/consistency_bench_2026-09-10.json and its _mw and _rf "
      "companions. {#tbl-scoreboard-bench}")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="The legacy centered variant and the weights-off ablation under the same probes (removed variant, diagnostic)"}
These rows establish one mechanism: a frame centered on the plain mean of
the sampled points collapses under a change of sampling law, and nothing
else in the model does, since the same checkpoint re-evaluated with a
measure-weighted center, or given the exact frame of the full geometry,
holds with ISLA.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scoreboard-legacy-consistency
#| output: asis
legacy = [
    ("legacy centered variant (plain-mean center)", R["isla_reference_constant_gauge"]["density_factor"], (B0, "iw_mt2_lr1e3"), (B0, "lad_hl_mt2_super_scarce")),
    ("the same checkpoint with a measure-weighted center", R["isla_constant_gauge_mcenter"]["density_factor"], (Bmc, "cg_dr_mt2_mcenter"), (Bmc, "cg_hl_mt2_mcenter_super_scarce")),
    ("the same checkpoint given the exact full-geometry frame", R["isla_frame_full_frame"]["density_factor"], None, None),
    ("weights-off ablation (never adopted)", R["isla_weights_off_ablation"]["density_factor"], (B0, "now_mt2_lr1e3"), (B0, "a35_hl_mt2_noweights")),
]
out = "| configuration (diagnostic) | 10:1 density bias, sample frame: biased ÷ uniform | 40,000 cells, DrivAerML: area / biased | 40,000 cells, HiLift 35 cases: area / biased |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\n"
for label, df, dr, hl in legacy:
    out += f"| {label} | {df:.2f}x | {cell(*dr) if dr else 'not run'} | {cell(*hl) if hl else 'not run'} |\n"
print(out)
print(": The legacy centered variant under the two consistency instruments of this section (exploration-budget checkpoints), and the "
      "weights-off ablation, which reads the mesher's cell pattern and collapses hardest of every "
      "configuration measured. Data: results/accuracy_consistency_matrix_2026-09-10.json; "
      "results/consistency_bench/consistency_bench_2026-09-10.json and its _mcenter companion. "
      "{#tbl-scoreboard-legacy-consistency}")
```
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="The similarity-gauge variant under the same probes (removed variant, diagnostic)"}
The similarity-gauge variant centers on the measure-weighted centroid and
scales by the RMS radius, both integrals of the sampled geometry, so it is
consistent under a change of sampling law like ISLA; what it adds is a
center estimated from the sample, which ISLA declines on principle. Its
price, on the surface at 435 cars: the price of not being told the body's
center is at most about 2%, inside seed noise (@sec-nb-sgref-verdict).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scoreboard-sg-consistency
#| output: asis
sgc = [("similarity-gauge variant (lr 1e-3)", R["isla_similarity_gauge_lr1e3"]["density_factor"], None, None),
       ("similarity-gauge variant (lr 3e-3)", None, (B0, "iw_mt2_gauge"), None)]
out = "| configuration (diagnostic) | 10:1 density bias, sample frame: biased ÷ uniform | 40,000 cells, DrivAerML: area / biased | 40,000 cells, HiLift 35 cases: area / biased |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\n"
for label, df, dr, hl in sgc:
    out += f"| {label} | {f'{df:.2f}x' if df else 'not run'} | {cell(*dr) if dr else 'not run'} | {cell(*hl) if hl else 'not run'} |\n"
print(out)
print(": The similarity-gauge variant under the two consistency instruments of this section (exploration-budget checkpoints). Data: "
      "results/accuracy_consistency_matrix_2026-09-10.json; "
      "results/consistency_bench/consistency_bench_2026-09-10.json. "
      "{#tbl-scoreboard-sg-consistency}")
```
:::

Read together, the two instruments say one thing: the sampling-law
dependence of every architecture lives in the input frame, not in the
attention. Measure weighting in the slice pooling repairs the aggregation
for the Transolver family at an in-distribution price that is being
re-measured at the reporting protocol (small on DrivAerML and larger on the
wings in the exploration runs); a frame that is a property of the geometry rather
than of the sample, whether ISLA's relative frame or a Horvitz–Thompson
centroid in the baselines' datapipe, removes the rest. The Horvitz–Thompson
centered GeoTransolver and Transolver are ablations that locate the
property; the public GeoTransolver and Transolver keep their plain-mean
frame (@sec-part-baseline), so the deployable comparison is GeoTransolver
and Transolver as released against ISLA.

A reader of @fig-scoreboard-density will ask why one would not simply use
GeoTransolver with ISLA's measure-weighted pooling and the
Horvitz–Thompson-centered datapipe. One could, and the figure is the
evidence that consistency under a change of sampling is not ISLA's property
alone: it belongs to two choices any slice-attention model can make, the
measure in the pooling and a frame taken from integrals of the surface. The
ablation's in-distribution price for them is being re-measured at the
reporting protocol (small in the exploration runs), and under the refinement
benchmark it is consistent at every count, and more consistent than ISLA
(@tbl-scoreboard-steelman). What it buys consistency with is a body
centroid: the datapipe centers every coordinate on the measure-weighted
centroid of the surface, a point the physics does not distinguish and that
is ill-posed for an open, truncated or multi-body boundary, and the model
then consumes absolute positions in that frame in every layer. That is the
construct ISLA declines (@sec-isla-variants). It also does not make the
model covariant: its pose behavior still comes from augmentation or a
canonical frame. The comparison the book makes is therefore not "consistent
against inconsistent" but "consistent and exactly covariant without any
centroid, at a measured price in distribution" against "consistent with a
centroid, position-informed, not covariant".

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scoreboard-steelman
#| output: asis
SM = J("steelman_reduction_2026-09-18.json")["arms"]
RFB = J("consistency_bench/consistency_bench_rf_2026-09-11.json")["arms"]["rf_dr_mt2_meas"]["table"]
def dev(arm, s, c): return SM[arm]["deviation_over_unif"][s][str(c)]["mean"]
out = "| model | uniform error, 10,000 cells | area ÷ uniform at 2,500 / 10,000 / 40,000 | biased ÷ uniform at 2,500 / 10,000 / 40,000 |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\n"
for arm, lab in (("gt_ht", "GeoTransolver + ISLA's measure-weighted pooling + Horvitz–Thompson-centered datapipe (ablation)"), ("t_ht", "Transolver + ISLA's measure-weighted pooling + Horvitz–Thompson-centered datapipe (ablation)")):
    out += f"| {lab} | {SM[arm]['table']['unif']['10000']['mean']:.4f} | " + " / ".join(f"{dev(arm,'area',c):.3f}" for c in (2500, 10000, 40000)) + " | " + " / ".join(f"{dev(arm,'biased',c):.3f}" for c in (2500, 10000, 40000)) + " |\n"
isla_u = {c: RFB["unif"][c]["pressure_l2"]["mean"] for c in ("10000", "40000")}
out += (f"| ISLA | {isla_u['10000']:.4f} | — / {RFB['area']['10000']['pressure_l2']['mean']/isla_u['10000']:.3f} / {RFB['area']['40000']['pressure_l2']['mean']/isla_u['40000']:.3f} "
        f"| — / {RFB['biased']['10000']['pressure_l2']['mean']/isla_u['10000']:.3f} / {RFB['biased']['40000']['pressure_l2']['mean']/isla_u['40000']:.3f} |\n")
print(out)
print(": The steel-man of the consistency claim: the two baseline ablations that adopt ISLA's measure semantics and an "
      "integral (Horvitz–Thompson) centroid, through the refinement benchmark (float32, 48 DrivAerML validation cars, "
      "two seeds each, seed means, exploration-budget checkpoints), with ISLA on the same benchmark for context. A deviation of 1.000 is exact consistency; "
      "the benchmark's bar is 3% at 40,000 cells. How to read this: the ablations are consistent at every count and more "
      "consistent than ISLA; the comparison ISLA makes is covariance and center-freeness on top of consistency, not "
      "consistency alone. ISLA's 2,500-cell row is not in its benchmark artifact. Data: results/steelman_reduction_2026-09-18.json; "
      "results/consistency_bench/consistency_bench_rf_2026-09-11.json. {#tbl-scoreboard-steelman}")
```

On the wings the relative frame's
convergence is measured on the fixed-angle split: from 2,500 to 40,000 cells
its area-sampler deviation falls from +45% to +2.6% and its biased-sampler
deviation from +81% to +5.5%, converging but not yet at the bias bar at
40,000, while it is the most accurate ISLA arm under every sampler at every
count (@sec-consistency-bench).

## The law the training sample is drawn by {#sec-scoreboard-training-law}

**Trained under the area-proportional sampling law and scored on the
independent uniform draw, GeoTransolver is 2.6x (wings) and 7.9x (cars)
worse than its uniform-trained twin and Transolver 2.4x and 9.6x, while ISLA
moves 1% and 8%: ISLA's trained function is weakly dependent on the law its
training sample was drawn by, the baselines' are dependent by factors.**
This is the other half of the discretization question, the half a
practitioner meets when a surrogate trained on one mesher's output is handed
a mesh from another; @sec-training-law has the figure (@fig-training-law),
the mechanism and the open question of why the cars show the larger
dependence. It is reproduced on both datasets.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scoreboard-training-law
#| output: asis
TW = J("trainarea_reduction_2026-09-20.json")["verdict"]; TC = J("trainarea_dr_reduction_2026-09-20.json")["verdict"]
out = "| model | HiLiftAeroML, 35 training cases, 200,000 cells | DrivAerML, 435 training cars, 100,000 cells |\n|---|---:|---:|\n"
for label, m in (("ISLA", "isla"), ("GeoTransolver", "gt_unit"), ("Transolver", "transolver_unit")):
    out += f"| {label} | {TW[f'{m}_area_over_uniform_unif']:.2f}x | {TC[f'{m}_area_over_uniform_unif']:.2f}x |\n"
print(out)
print(": The training-law change on two datasets: surface-pressure error of the checkpoint trained under the area-proportional Poisson law divided by "
      "that of the same configuration trained under the uniform-over-cells law, both scored on the same validation surfaces under the independent uniform draw "
      "(float32, two seeds, seed means; each architecture at its reporting-protocol rate). How to read this: 1 means the trained function does not depend on the "
      "law its training sample was drawn by; the wing column is at the reporting protocol, the car column at the 100,000-cell scaling budget (cells are flat above "
      "100,000, @sec-scoreboard-tokens). The figure and per-arm values are @fig-training-law. Data: results/trainarea_reduction_2026-09-20.json; "
      "results/trainarea_dr_reduction_2026-09-20.json. {#tbl-scoreboard-training-law}")
```

## The floor both architectures reach {#sec-scoreboard-floor}

**Given width and depth, ISLA and GeoTransolver reach the same floor of
about 0.040 on DrivAerML at 435 cars: ISLA 0.0407 at 68M parameters (384
wide, 24 layers, cosine routing) and 0.0405 at 136M (48 layers),
GeoTransolver 0.0406 at 143M (1,024 wide) and 0.0403 at 571M (2,048 wide,
estimated parameters); at matched parameters of about 140M the two are the
same to within 0.1%, and ISLA comes within 1% of the floor at half
GeoTransolver's parameters and about half of GeoTransolver-1,024's training
memory.**
This is one dataset's result at the 100,000-cell scaling budget; the
picture, with every ladder on one axis of parameter count, is
@fig-capacity, and the wing twin is pending (@sec-program-status). Two
things decide how each architecture gets there. GeoTransolver's width ladder
saturates (6.7%, 2.6% and 0.7% per doubling from 256 to 2,048 wide). ISLA's
width ladder turns over above 768 under either routing form, so its axis is
depth, and depth is reachable only under cosine routing: linear routing has
a learning-rate ceiling that falls like 1/width and at least 1/depth, above
which the loss rises to the mean-field plateau, and 48 layers has no clean
linear rate (@sec-lr-protocol). The memory column is where ISLA's advantage
lies: its best configuration at or under each training-memory budget is at
least as accurate as GeoTransolver's at every budget measured, by 9% at 40
GB, 1.4% from 51 to 86 GB and parity at 100 GB.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scoreboard-floor
#| output: asis
CFG = J("cap435_reduction_2026-09-20.json")["configurations"]
CFI = J("cap435_interim_2026-09-20.json")["configurations"]   # the same lanes with peak training memory recorded
RNC = J("routenorm_interim_2026-09-20.json")["configurations"]
EXT = J("routenorm_extension_2026-09-21.json")["configurations"]
ISO = J("isocost_reduction_2026-09-20.json")
def memcell(key, star=False):
    m = CFI.get(key, {}).get("peak_mem_gb")
    return ("—" if m is None else f"{m:.0f}" + ("\\*" if star else ""))
def P(n, est=False): return f"{n/1e6:.0f}M" + (" (estimated)" if est else "")
rows = [
    ("ISLA", "linear", "192 × 12", CFG["isla|w192|d12|s256|lr1e-3"]["params"], "1e-3", CFG["isla|w192|d12|s256|lr1e-3"]["pressure_l2_mean"], memcell("isla|w192|d12|s256|lr1e-3")),
    ("ISLA", "linear", "384 × 12", CFG["isla|w384|d12|s256|lr5e-4"]["params"], "5e-4", CFG["isla|w384|d12|s256|lr5e-4"]["pressure_l2_mean"], memcell("isla|w384|d12|s256|lr5e-4")),
    ("ISLA", "cosine", "384 × 12", CFG["isla|w384|d12|s256|lr5e-4"]["params"], "5e-4", RNC["cars|cos|w384|lr5e-4"]["mean"], memcell("isla|w384|d12|s256|lr5e-4", True)),
    ("ISLA", "cosine", "768 × 12", CFG["isla|w768|d12|s256|lr2.5e-4"]["params"], "5e-4", RNC["cars|cos|w768|lr5e-4"]["mean"], memcell("isla|w768|d12|s256|lr2.5e-4", True)),
    ("**ISLA**", "cosine", "384 × 24", EXT["isla|cos|w384|d24|lr5e-4"]["params"], "5e-4", EXT["isla|cos|w384|d24|lr5e-4"]["pressure_l2_mean"], memcell("isla|w384|d24|s256|lr5e-4", True)),
    ("**ISLA**", "cosine", "384 × 48", EXT["isla|cos|w384|d48|lr2.5e-4"]["params"], "2.5e-4", EXT["isla|cos|w384|d48|lr2.5e-4"]["pressure_l2_mean"], memcell("isla|w384|d48|s256|lr5e-4", True)),
    ("GeoTransolver", "—", "512 × 12", CFG["gt|w512|d12|s256|lr3e-3"]["params"], "3e-3", CFG["gt|w512|d12|s256|lr3e-3"]["pressure_l2_mean"], memcell("gt|w512|d12|s256|lr3e-3")),
    ("GeoTransolver", "—", "512 × 24", CFG["gt|w512|d24|s256|lr3e-3"]["params"], "3e-3", CFG["gt|w512|d24|s256|lr3e-3"]["pressure_l2_mean"], memcell("gt|w512|d24|s256|lr3e-3")),
    ("**GeoTransolver**", "—", "1,024 × 12", CFG["gt|w1024|d12|s256|lr1e3"]["params"], "1e-3", CFG["gt|w1024|d12|s256|lr1e3"]["pressure_l2_mean"], memcell("gt|w1024|d12|s256|lr1e3")),
    ("**GeoTransolver**", "—", "2,048 × 12", EXT["gt|w2048|d12|lr1e-3"]["params"], "1e-3", EXT["gt|w2048|d12|lr1e-3"]["pressure_l2_mean"], "—"),
]
out = "| architecture | routing | width × layers | parameters | training cells | rate | error | peak training memory [GB] |\n|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n"
for arch, rt, shape, p, lr, err, mem in rows:
    out += f"| {arch} | {rt} | {shape} | {P(p, est=(shape == '2,048 × 12'))} | 100,000 | {lr} | {err:.4f} | {mem} |\n"
print(out)
fm = ISO["bars"]["iso_memory_frontier"]
print(": The floor on DrivAerML (435 training cars, 48 validation cars, float32 surface-pressure error, two-seed means, 500 epochs) at the 100,000-cell scaling budget, "
      "single dataset. Each row is one trained configuration at its best clean rate; the bold rows are the two architectures at or within 1% of the floor. "
      "Peak training memory is the recorded peak of the lane on one GB300 at batch 1; entries marked \\* are the linear-routing lane of the same shape "
      "(the routing form changes no tensor shape) and the 2,048-wide GeoTransolver lane's memory and exact parameter count were not recorded (the count is "
      "extrapolated from the measured 256-to-1,024 ladder). How to read this: the table is a floor, not a scaling law; ISLA's width ladder beyond 768 and "
      "GeoTransolver's are in @fig-capacity, and on the accuracy-against-memory frontier the best ISLA at or under each budget is at least as accurate as the best "
      f"GeoTransolver at every budget measured (GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA at least {fm['min_gt_over_isla']:.3f}, at {fm['at_budget_gb']:.0f} GB). Data: results/cap435_reduction_2026-09-20.json; "
      "results/cap435_interim_2026-09-20.json (memory); results/routenorm_interim_2026-09-20.json; results/routenorm_extension_2026-09-21.json; "
      "results/isocost_reduction_2026-09-20.json. {#tbl-scoreboard-floor}")
```

## The standing against the cell budget {#sec-scoreboard-tokens}

**Above 100,000 cells per case every model's error is flat in the cell
count, so the reporting protocol's 200,000 cells is a converged budget, and
the full-data gap that smaller counts show on DrivAerML is a property of
the count.** @tbl-scoreboard-cells trains and scores each architecture at its
protocol width from 100,000 to 600,000 cells per case; the fitted exponent
of error against cells is `{python} f"{J('isocost_reduction_2026-09-20.json')['bars']['cells_exponent']['alpha_isla']:.2f}"` for ISLA and
`{python} f"{J('isocost_reduction_2026-09-20.json')['bars']['cells_exponent']['alpha_gt']:.2f}"` for GeoTransolver, and doubling the
epochs to 1,000 at 200,000 cells moves neither by more than 0.1%
(results/isocost_reduction_2026-09-20.json). The gain from denser sampling
is spent by 100,000 cells; what buys accuracy past it is width and depth
(@sec-scoreboard-floor).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scoreboard-cells
#| output: asis
IC = ISO["configurations"]
def ic(model, w, c, lr):
    k = f"{model}|w{w}|c{c}|lr{lr}|ep500"; d = IC.get(k)
    return (f"{d['pressure_l2_mean']:.4f}" if d and d.get("pressure_l2_mean") else "not run")
out = "| cells per case (train and score) | ISLA, width 192 (1e-3) | GeoTransolver, width 256 (3e-3) | Transolver, width 256 (3e-3) |\n|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n"
for c in ("100k", "200k", "400k", "600k"):
    out += f"| {int(c[:-1]):,},000 | {ic('isla', 192, c, '1e-3')} | {ic('gt_unit', 256, c, '3e-3')} | {ic('transolver_unit', 256, c, '3e-3')} |\n"
print(out)
print(": Surface-pressure error (area-weighted relative L2, float32, 48 DrivAerML validation cars, 435 training cars, 500 epochs, two-seed means) when every model "
      "trains and is scored at the same cell count, each architecture at its protocol width and reporting-protocol rate. How to read this: the rows differ by under "
      "1% within a column, so the cell count above 100,000 is not an axis of accuracy for any of the three; the 200,000-cell row is the reporting protocol of "
      "@tbl-scoreboard-200k (the lanes differ, the values agree within seed noise). Data: results/isocost_reduction_2026-09-20.json. {#tbl-scoreboard-cells}")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="The path from 10,000 to 80,000 cells (legacy centered variant, removed; diagnostic)"}
Between the exploration budget and 100,000 cells the DrivAerML ratio moves
from 0.90 to 0.985 against GeoTransolver and past parity against Transolver.
The only ISLA trained at 40,000 and 80,000 cells at width 192 is the legacy
centered variant; its 10,000-cell value is within 1% of ISLA's on this
dataset, so the ratios read across.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scoreboard-tokens
#| output: asis
TP = J("tokproto_reduction_2026-09-18.json")
r10 = TP["ratios_10k"]
out = "| cells per case (train and score) | GeoTransolver | Transolver | ISLA (legacy centered variant) | GeoTransolver ÷ variant | Transolver ÷ variant |\n|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n"
out += f"| 10,000 | {mean(S['dr435']['gt']):.4f} | {mean(S['dr435']['t']):.4f} | {mean(S['dr435']['isla_cg']):.4f} | {r10['gt_over_isla']:.3f} | {r10['t_over_isla']:.3f} |\n"
for c in ("40000", "80000"):

      "parentheses. The ISLA arm is the legacy centered variant at every count (the only ISLA trained at 40,000 and 80,000). How to read this: the ratio moves toward and past parity with the budget; the "
      "reporting protocol's 200,000-cell standing on ISLA itself is @tbl-scoreboard-200k. Data: "
```

## Resources behind the comparison {#sec-scoreboard-resources}

**At the protocol widths (ISLA 192, GeoTransolver and Transolver 256) the
three architectures are parameter-matched, and ISLA trains in the least
memory once its geometry is recomputed in the backward pass.**
@tbl-scoreboard-resources measures the eager path on which all three can be
run on one instrument; on the compiled path the recipe runs, ISLA's
training step is 1.05x GeoTransolver's at 10,000 tokens with the recompute
on and 0.86x without, at half the memory (@sec-isla-cost).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scoreboard-resources
#| output: asis
def cfg(name, tokens):
    return next(c for c in cost["configs"] if c["name"] == name and c["tokens"] == tokens)
rows = [("ISLA, hidden 192", "isla_h192_fast_plain"),
        ("ISLA, hidden 192, geometry recomputed in the backward pass (the recipe's default)", "isla_h192_fast_ckpt"),
        ("GeoTransolver, hidden 256", "gt_h256"),
        ("Transolver, hidden 256", "transolver_h256")]
out = "| configuration | parameters | step at 10,000 tokens [ms] | peak memory at 10,000 tokens [GiB] | step at 80,000 tokens [ms] | peak memory at 80,000 tokens [GiB] |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n"
for label, name in rows:
    a, b = cfg(name, 10000), cfg(name, 80000)
    out += (f"| {label} | {a['n_params']/1e6:.1f}M | {statistics.median(a['step_ms']):.0f} | {max(a['incremental_peak_allocated_bytes'])/2**30:.2f} "
            f"| {statistics.median(b['step_ms']):.0f} | {max(b['incremental_peak_allocated_bytes'])/2**30:.1f} |\n")
print(out)
print(": Training cost of the three architectures on one instrument and one execution path: one "
      "GB300 GPU, eager execution, batch of one case, bfloat16 autocast, AdamW step, median of five "
      "measured steps after three warm-up steps; memory is the peak allocated during the step net of "
      "the resident parameters and optimizer state. The recomputed-geometry row is the same function at "
      "a lower memory and a higher step time. How to read this: the eager path ranks the models on one instrument; the compiled path the recipe trains on is in @tbl-isla-cost. "
      "Data: results/isla_vs_baselines_cost_fastkernel_2026-09-09.json. {#tbl-scoreboard-resources}")
```

The token budget decides the cost comparison more than the architecture
does. @fig-cost-sweep sweeps the training step from 2,500 to 200,000 tokens
per case on the compiled path every model trains on. GeoTransolver's step is
nearly flat below 40,000 tokens, where the GPU is not saturated, and grows
to about twice its 10,000-token value at the recipe's default of 200,000;
ISLA on its default path (geometry recomputed in the backward pass) grows
linearly from 20,000 tokens on and is five times GeoTransolver's step at
200,000, while ISLA with the fused geometry kernel tracks GeoTransolver's
step at every count in less than half its memory. At the recipe default of
200,000 cells every model fits one GB300 with room to spare; GeoTransolver's
49 GiB would not fit an 80 GB card.

```{python}
#| label: fig-cost-sweep
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Error (top), training-step time (middle) and peak allocated memory
#|   (bottom) against the number of tokens per case. Top: surface-pressure
#|   error of each model at its recipe width (ISLA 192, GeoTransolver 256,
#|   Transolver 256) trained and scored at the token count on the x axis, 435
#|   DrivAerML cars, 500 epochs, float32, two-seed means with the seeds as
#|   short bars; the panel is empty below 100,000 tokens because the program
#|   reports no accuracy at coarser budgets. Middle and bottom: one GB300,
#|   bf16 autocast, batch of one case, AdamW step included, every model
#|   compiled, median of ten measured steps after warm-up on random inputs;
#|   ISLA on its recipe-default path (geometry recomputed in the backward
#|   pass) and with the opt-in fused geometry kernel (open squares, dashed).
#|   How to read this: all axes are logarithmic and the lines are joined
#|   measurements, not fits; the cost sweep measures the step alone and stops
#|   at 200,000 tokens, while the error ladder runs to 400,000 (600,000 for
#|   ISLA), and the training lanes of this book are dominated by data
#|   loading, so the cost panels rank the models' step cost, not their
#|   wall-clock. The 200,000-token column is the recipe's default budget.
#|   Data: results/cost_sweep_gb300_bf16_2026-09-18.json;
#|   results/isocost_reduction_2026-09-20.json.
#| code-fold: true
import statistics as st
CS = J("cost_sweep_gb300_bf16_2026-09-18.json")["runs"]
ISO = J("isocost_reduction_2026-09-20.json")["configurations"]
arms = [("isla_compiled_recompute", "isla_ref", "ISLA (recipe default path)", {}),
        ("isla_fused_compiled", "isla_ref", "ISLA + fused geometry kernel", dict(ls="--", mfc="white")),
        ("geotransolver_compiled", "gt", "GeoTransolver", {}),
        ("transolver_compiled", "t", "Transolver", {})]
fig, (axe, ax0, ax1) = plt.subplots(3, 1, figsize=(8.0, 9.4), sharex=True, gridspec_kw=dict(hspace=0.08, height_ratios=[1.1, 1, 1]))
for model, key, width in (("isla", "isla_ref", 192), ("gt_unit", "gt", 256), ("transolver_unit", "t", 256)):
    rows = sorted([c for c in ISO.values() if c["model"] == model and c["width"] == width and c["epochs"] == 500
                   and any("pressure_l2" in r for r in c["runs"].values())], key=lambda c: c["cells"])
    xs = [c["cells"] for c in rows]
    ys = [st.mean([r["pressure_l2"] for r in c["runs"].values() if "pressure_l2" in r]) for c in rows]
    axe.plot(xs, ys, **series_kwargs(key, label=f"{STYLE[key]['label']}, {width} wide"))
    for c, x in zip(rows, xs):
        axe.plot([x] * len(c["runs"]), [r["pressure_l2"] for r in c["runs"].values() if "pressure_l2" in r], ls="none", marker="_", color=STYLE[key]["color"], ms=8, mew=1.2)
axe.set_yscale("log"); axe.set_ylim(0.040, 0.050); axe.set_yticks([0.040, 0.042, 0.044, 0.046, 0.048, 0.050]); axe.set_yticklabels(["0.040", "0.042", "0.044", "0.046", "0.048", "0.050"])
axe.yaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter()); axe.set_ylabel("surface-pressure\nrelative L2 error [–]")
axe.text(5000, 0.0492, "no accuracy reported below 100,000 tokens", fontsize=8.5, color=INK2, va="top")
axe.legend(loc="lower right", fontsize=8.5)
for arm, key, lab, ov in arms:
    rows = sorted([r for r in CS if r["arm"] == arm and r["status"] == "ok"], key=lambda r: r["tokens"])
    xs = [r["tokens"] for r in rows]
    ax0.plot(xs, [st.median(r["step_ms"]) for r in rows], **series_kwargs(key, label=lab, **ov))
    ax1.plot(xs, [r["peak_allocated_gib"] for r in rows], **series_kwargs(key, label=lab, **ov))
for ax in (axe, ax0, ax1):
    ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.grid(True, which="major", color=GRID); ax.grid(False, which="minor")
    ax.axvline(200000, color=BASELINE, lw=1.0, zorder=0)
ax0.set_yscale("log"); ax1.set_yscale("log")
ax0.set_ylabel("training step [ms]"); ax1.set_ylabel("peak allocated memory [GiB]")
ax0.set_yticks([20, 50, 100, 200, 500]); ax0.set_yticklabels(["20", "50", "100", "200", "500"])
ax1.set_yticks([0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50]); ax1.set_yticklabels(["0.5", "1", "2", "5", "10", "20", "50"])
ax1.set_xticks([2500, 10000, 40000, 100000, 200000, 400000]); ax1.set_xticklabels(["2,500", "10,000", "40,000", "100,000", "200,000", "400,000"])
ax1.xaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter()); ax0.yaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter()); ax1.yaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter())
ax1.set_xlabel("tokens per case [count]")
axe.text(200000, 0.0492, " recipe default", fontsize=8, color=INK2, va="top")
ax0.legend(loc="upper left", fontsize=8.5)
axe.set_title("error and training-step cost against token count (435 DrivAerML cars; one GB300, bf16, batch 1, compiled)")
plt.show()
```

## Rungs pending at the reporting protocol {#sec-scoreboard-exploration}

**Every standing in this chapter is measured at the reporting protocol;
the rungs the program explored at 10,000 cells and has not yet re-measured
at 200,000 are listed here as pending, and their 10,000-cell values are not
quoted.** The list is what remains of the exploration board once the rows
with a reporting-protocol twin are stated above; it ranks nothing.

### Surface rungs without a reporting-protocol twin {#sec-scoreboard-surface}

| setting | GeoTransolver | Transolver | ISLA | status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HiLiftAeroML, 210 training cases (180 validation cases) | training at 200,000 cells | training | training | pending at the reporting protocol |
| HiLiftAeroML, 21 training geometries (18 held-out geometries, 180 cases) | training | training | training | pending |
| HiLiftAeroML, 510 training cases (180 validation cases) | measured at 10,000 cells only | measured at 10,000 cells only | never trained at any budget | pending; no ISLA arm yet |
| HiLiftAeroML, 1,260 training cases (180 validation cases) | measured at 10,000 and 20,000 cells only | measured at 10,000 cells only | never trained at any budget | pending; no ISLA arm yet |

: The surface rungs without a reporting-protocol measurement. How to read this: the rows are configurations, not results; the 35-case, 4-geometry and fixed-angle rungs are in @tbl-scoreboard-200k-wings and the DrivAerML rungs in @tbl-scoreboard-200k. Where a cell says "measured at 10,000 cells only" the value is an exploration-run number and is not quoted; on the 510- and 1,260-case rungs the ISLA arm of the exploration runs was the removed legacy centered variant, so ISLA has no measurement there at any budget. The live status of each lane is in @sec-program-status. {#tbl-scoreboard-surface}

Two configurations are deliberately not rows at any budget. GeoTransolver
and Transolver with ISLA's measure-weighted pooling, ablations that carry
the same quadrature measure in their slice pooling that ISLA does, locate
the property measured in @sec-scoreboard-consistency and are not
modifications of the released models; their in-distribution price is
pending at the reporting protocol. The ISLA weights-off ablation is not a
row because it is not a configuration the program adopts: it gains on the
wing rungs by reading the mesher's cell pattern, and under a change of
sampling it collapses hardest of every configuration measured
(@sec-scoreboard-consistency, @sec-limits-mechanism).

### The sealed deflection split {#sec-scoreboard-other}

**The one surface setting that does not fit the ladders, the wing
deflection split, is pending at the reporting protocol.** It trains on the
80% of geometries with the milder flap-and-slat settings and evaluates
once, sealed, on the 20% most aggressive (@sec-limits-regime), with
GeoTransolver against ISLA. Its exploration-run reading
(results/deflection_sealed_test_2026-09-15.json) is not quoted; the
200,000-cell lanes are training (@sec-program-status), and the sealed test
is evaluated once per checkpoint when they finish.

## What is not yet on the board {#sec-scoreboard-pending}

**Three measurements are live and would change or complete rows above:
the wing half of the cosine-routing study, which decides whether cosine
routing becomes ISLA's default (the DrivAerML half is in
@tbl-scoreboard-floor and @tbl-scoreboard-200k-interior); the wing scaling
picture, the second-dataset twin of @tbl-scoreboard-floor; and the remaining
HiLiftAeroML rungs at the reporting protocol (the 210-, 510- and 1,260-case
rungs, the geometry ladders and the deflection split), which join
@tbl-scoreboard-200k-wings as they report.** Two gaps are not being
measured: ISLA below full data on the DrivAerML interior ladder, known only
on the removed similarity-gauge variant (the collapsed note in
@sec-scoreboard-interior), and
GeoTransolver's and Transolver's consistency with a Horvitz–Thompson
centroid on the wings, measured on DrivAerML only and only as an ablation.
The live status of each item, with its preregistered bar, is in
@sec-program-status.

way and scored on the standard uniform interior sample, the arm is worse
than the similarity-gauge interior variant (diagnostic) it was built from on

viscosity
